text:
maria: heads-up — seeing intermittent NXDOMAINs from GPU nodes in us-west when they try to fetch models from internal-model-fetch.svc.redwood. ~5% of pods returned NXDOMAIN for the svc name, started ~10m after the kube-proxy iptables rollout.

aj: did the nodes switch to systemd-resolved / 127.0.0.53 stub? that usually changes behavior for short names.

maria: yep, lots of nodes show `/etc/resolv.conf` pointing at 127.0.0.53. attaching a snippet:

```
search svc.cluster.local cluster.local redwood.internal
nameserver 127.0.0.53
options ndots:5 timeout:2 rotate
```

devon: paste of a failing dig from one GPU node:

```
$ dig +short internal-model-fetch.svc.redwood @127.0.0.53
;; connection timed out; no servers could be reached
$ dig +short internal-model-fetch.svc.redwood
;; -> NXDOMAIN
```

paul: hunch — with `ndots:5` and our long search path, queries might be getting suffixed and walking through the search list, hitting an edge forwarder that has split-horizon config. negative caching TTL might be long on that forwarder. can we confirm which forwarder handled the NXDOMAIN?

maria: running `systemd-resolve --status` on node shows the stub forwarding to local node-local-dns (DaemonSet) which forwards to edge forwarders. attaching last hop logs from node-local-dns: `forwarder_apex: got NXDOMAIN from 10.8.7.11 (edge-ffwd-usw)`

aj: dns-prober-bot shows a recent config change — an env update to edge-forwarder that toggled authoritative / recursive handling in us-west 5h ago. also saw a config push to kube-proxy earlier which changed conntrack reuse. could be two orthogonal changes combining.

maria: symptoms — short-lived, flappy, mostly model fetches during cold starts. pods that retry immediately succeed. looks like negative cache/TTL is the main pain.

paul: quick mitigation: reduce negative-cache TTL on the forwarders for internal zones to 5s, and set node-local-dns to respect that. also consider increasing `ndots` client-side to 1 for fully-qualified queries from fetcher lib. but that's a code change.

devon: rolling node-local-dns restart on a small subset now: `kubectl rollout restart ds/node-local-dns -n kube-system --grace-period=30` — watch probe.

maria: @aj can you check SNAT port usage on the nodes? we saw earlier that when SNAT ports exhaust, some UDP queries dropped and fallback to TCP is delayed, which magnifies resolver failures.

aj: checking -> ephemeral port usage spiked during roll but under threshold. conntrack shows a bunch of TIME_WAIT but not exhausted. still, iptables change did change source-port randomization slightly.

dns-prober-bot: automated probe: "split-horizon mismatch: internal-model-fetch.svc.redwood resolves to 10.9.x.x in us-west forwarder A, but forwarder B returned NXDOMAIN for the same query; negative TTL observed 60s"

paul: plan: 1) rollback the kube-proxy iptables tweak in the next hour (canary) 2) patch forwarders to lower negative TTL for internal zones 3) keep node-local-dns restart canaryed 4) add short-term client retry jitter in model fetcher lib 5) create an eval to watch NXDOMAIN rate and model fetch latency.

maria: added to oncall rotation, assigning to @dev-oncall. will update with rollout results in this thread. :thumbsup:

devon: canary restart finished on 3 nodes, NXDOMAIN rate dropped from 4.8% -> 0.7% for those nodes. waiting on forwarder TTL patch.

maria: thanks — filing followups: infra ticket INFRA-3429 (rollback audit + forwarder patch), and SRE runbook note about ndots/searchpath interactions with stub resolvers.

paul: also putting a short-term alert on "internal svc NXDOMAIN rate" so we catch regression.

maria: closing for now, reopening if spike returns. :pray:
